newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark seen under pressure near-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark seen under pressure near-term.

text.p: The dollar's failure to push past resistance at 1.7210 marks, the March 6 high, combined with other unsustained intraday probes higher this week suggests dollar/mark will fall over the next few trading sessions, technical analysts said on Thursday.
"We were able to break above to new highs, but weren't able to follow through. That's a fairly negative sign for the next day or two," said David Solin, a partner at Foreign Exchange Analytics.
"I suspect we will work our way back down to 1.71 and change -- maybe even all the way back to 1.6955," he said.
After sliding sharply on Monday, dollar/mark hit a low of 1.6950, its lowest level this week.
On the upside, the dollar must break Thursday's 1.7210 cap, Friday's high at 1.7250/55, and resistance from last week at 1.73, before besting its April 15 three-year high of 1.7375 marks.

Against the yen, the dollar was boxed into a now-familiar 125.80 to 126.50 range. The technical outlook for dollar/yen remains bullish, but analysts expected sideways trade until after the Group of Seven leaders meet on Sunday in Washington.
"(Dollar/yen) will stay quiet through this week and after the G7, after no major announcement and no major change in policy, we probably go higher again," Solin said.
The dollar reached a 56-month high of 127.16 yen on April 10.
Sterling rebounded and approached resistance at $1.63 on Thursday, after sliding beneath support at $1.62 during European and early U.S. trade.
On Wednesday, the pound sold off sharply, breaking support at $1.6310 to hit a low of $1.6193.

"It appears now that you're not going to close below $1.62, which takes some of the sting out of what happened yesterday," said Robert Zukowski, senior capital markets technical analyst at Pegasus Econometric Group.
"Inter-day oscillators did generate new buy signals on the day after forming a bullish divergence," he added.
The dollar fell to 1.7150/60 marks at the U.S. midday from 1.7185/95 at the open and 125.90/00 yen from 126.08/18.
